original_question: Let Ω be the tiling space of an aperiodic repetitive tiling of dimension d, and let p(n) count patches of radius n up to translation. If p(n)=O(n^d), must the rational Čech cohomology of Ω be finitely generated, equivalently must rk(H^*(Ω,Q)) be finite?
target_in_paper: Section 2.5, Problem 2.5.1 (A. Julien: Relationship Between Complexity and Cohomology)
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual open problem. It correctly captures the ambient objects (an aperiodic repetitive tiling, its tiling space Ω, and dimension d), the growth hypothesis p(n)=O(n^d), the rational coefficient field Q, and the desired conclusion that the total rational cohomology should have finite rank. It also keeps the direction of implication correct: the paper asks only whether low complexity forces finite rational cohomology, not a full equivalence in general.
missing_details: The paper states the problem for dimension d≥1 explicitly.
The nearby context defines p(n) as the complexity function counting patches of radius n up to translation.

The official formulation is about the cohomology H^*(Ω, Q) in the paper’s usual notation; the word Čech is not used in Problem 2.5.1 itself, even though that is standard in the tiling-space literature.
To be fully paper-faithful, the question should be framed as a higher-dimensional generalization of the one-dimensional result cited just before it: for d=1, p(n)=O(n) implies rk(H^1(Ω, Q))<∞.

The paper explicitly contrasts this with the canonical cut-and-project case, where one has an equivalence p(n)=O(n^d) iff rk(H^*(Ω, Q))<∞; outside that setup, only the forward implication is being asked.
The coefficient field Q is essential: the paper immediately notes that the analogous statement over Z already fails in dimension 1 (via the Thue–Morse example).
The target is the total cohomology H^*(Ω, Q), i.e. finite total rank across all degrees, not just degree 1 except in the motivating one-dimensional result.
refined_question: Let T be an aperiodic, repetitive tiling of dimension d≥1, let Ω be its tiling space, and let p(n) denote the number of patches of radius n in T up to translation. Is it true that p(n)=O(n^d) implies rk(H^*(Ω, Q))<∞?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does polynomial patch complexity of order d force the rational cohomology groups of the tiling space Ω to be finitely generated?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly the open problem stated in Section 2.5 as Problem 2.5.1. The surrounding context first defines the complexity function in higher dimensions as counting radius-n patches up to translation, then recalls that for canonical cut-and-project tilings one has the equivalence p(n)=O(n^d) iff rk(H^*(Ω, Q))<∞, and then notes that outside the cut-and-project setting the reverse implication fails in general, while the case d=1 gives a positive converse p(n)=O(n) ⇒ rk(H^1(Ω, Q))<∞. Problem 2.5.1 asks whether this converse extends to arbitrary aperiodic repetitive tilings in higher dimension. The refined question keeps exactly that scope, preserves the coefficient field Q, and does not broaden the paper’s one-way implication into a general equivalence.
